subject: Materials Science
title: Precipitation Hardening
description: A fast breakdown of Precipitation Hardening for builders.

hook.text: In 1906 Alfred Wilm left aluminum samples over a weekend. They came back harder.

buildup.text: Tiny clusters of atoms had precipitated inside the metal, forming invisible obstacles.

discovery.text: These nano-sized precipitates pin dislocations — the defects that let metals deform.

twist.text: Too much aging overcoarsens the precipitates and the metal softens again.

climax.text: Aircraft aluminum alloys rely on precise aging — hours at exact temperatures.

punchline.text: The strongest aluminum is hardened by particles you can't see.

quiz.question: What causes precipitation hardening?
options: The metal is coated with a harder material
The metal is cooled to absolute zero
